question: If $A$ is the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} m & n & 1 \\ 1 & m & n \\ n & 1 & m \end{bmatrix}$ and $|A| = 0$, show that $m^3 + n^3 + 1 = 3mn$.
explanation:
Let's compute the determinant:

$|A| = \begin{vmatrix} m & n & 1 \\ 1 & m & n \\ n & 1 & m \end{vmatrix}$

Expand along the first row:

$= m \begin{vmatrix} m & n \\ 1 & m \end{vmatrix} - n \begin{vmatrix} 1 & n \\ n & m \end{vmatrix} + 1 \begin{vmatrix} 1 & m \\ n & 1 \end{vmatrix}$

Calculate minors:

$\begin{vmatrix} m & n \\ 1 & m \end{vmatrix}=m^2-n$

$\begin{vmatrix} 1 & n \\ n & m \end{vmatrix}=m-n^2$

$\begin{vmatrix} 1 & m \\ n & 1 \end{vmatrix}=1-mn$

So $|A|= m(m^2-n) - n(m-n^2) + (1-mn)$

$= m^3-mn - m n+ n^3 + 1 - m n$

$= m^3+n^3+1-3 m n$

Set $= 0 \implies m^3+n^3+1 = 3m n$
